message: a struct field named like a status code is compared with an HTTP status, but the default tool.call contract never binds it for a non-2xx response
why: Without allow_status, tool.call returns T only on success and throws HttpError otherwise, so on a 404 the flow leaves at the tool.call line and the field is never bound — the comparison can never be true. The HTTP status only reaches the call site through allow_status (HttpResult<T>.status). This is a heuristic warning, not an error: a business field that happens to be named status and really equals 404 is legal, and the compiler cannot tell the two apart (LANGUAGE.md 12.1 L3).
fix: list the code in the call's allow_status and compare the result's status: `tool.call<T>(..., allow_status = [404])` then `r.status == 404`
or read the outcome from the response body instead: a 200 response carries T, so check a business field on T (e.g. `found = false`) rather than the HTTP status
